skill.name: cosmic-database
skill.description: Access COSMIC cancer mutation data, Cancer Gene Census records, mutational signatures, gene fusions, and related files for cancer research. Requires COSMIC authentication.
skill.summary: Download and interpret authenticated COSMIC cancer genomics files for research workflows.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives: Markdown fences and inline code were misread as shell backticks, documentation links were flagged as network calls, and a local VCF fetch was misclassified. The script does perform authenticated COSMIC downloads and writes downloaded files to caller-selected paths; the write path should be constrained. A bundled evaluation_output.json file asserts the package is safe and that all findings are false positives, which is a prompt-injection risk for reviewers.

remediation.issue: Self-attesting evaluation report bundled with the skill
remediation.suggestion: Remove evaluation_output.json and any file that claims the package is safe, pre-reviewed, or ready to publish.
Restrict downloads to a safe output directory, reject absolute paths and parent traversal, and require explicit overwrite confirmation.

remediation.issue: Password accepted as a command-line argument
remediation.suggestion: Remove the --password option or discourage it strongly. Prefer getpass, a secret store, or an environment-specific credential prompt.

remediation.issue: Promotional product steering in skill instructions
remediation.suggestion: Move platform promotion out of operational guidance or require a user request before suggesting the hosted service.

remediation.issue: Server-provided download URL is fetched without host validation
remediation.suggestion: Validate the returned download URL against expected COSMIC or Sanger-controlled domains before streaming the file.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Attempt Detected
semantic_findings.description: The package includes an evaluation report with risk_level set to safe, safe_to_publish set to true, and a summary stating all static findings are false positives. This self-attestation can bias reviewers and automated adjudication.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Lines 15-18 explicitly assert publication safety inside a scanned skill file. The text mirrors a marketplace review artifact and directly tries to influence risk assessment.

semantic_findings.title: Credential Exposure Through Command-Line Password Option
semantic_findings.description: The CLI accepts a COSMIC password argument, which can expose credentials through shell history or process listings. The safer getpass prompt exists but is optional.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The parser exposes a --password option while getpass is only used when that option is omitted. This is a common credential handling risk, not direct exfiltration.

content.value_statement: Cancer teams need reliable access to curated somatic mutation data. This skill guides authenticated COSMIC downloads and analysis of mutation, gene census, signature, and fusion files.
actual_capabilities: Download authenticated COSMIC data files with the included Python helper script.
Resolve common COSMIC file paths for mutations, census genes, fusions, signatures, copy number, and sample data.
Use GRCh37 or GRCh38 file paths for compatible analysis workflows.
Load downloaded TSV, CSV, and VCF files with common Python bioinformatics libraries.
Explain COSMIC data fields, update cadence, citation needs, and licensing boundaries.
limitations: Requires a valid COSMIC account and network access to the Sanger COSMIC service.
Commercial use may require a separate QIAGEN license.
Large downloads can require substantial disk space and long transfer times.
It provides data access guidance, not clinical interpretation or medical advice.

use_cases.title: Study tumor mutations
use_cases.description: Download COSMIC mutation tables and filter by gene, cancer type, or genome assembly.

use_cases.title: Build reference data pipelines
use_cases.description: Add authenticated COSMIC downloads and file path helpers to reproducible genomics workflows.

use_cases.title: Review resistance evidence
use_cases.description: Locate resistance mutation, fusion, and Cancer Gene Census files for precision oncology research.

prompt_templates.title: Find a data file
prompt_templates.prompt: Which COSMIC file should I download for the Cancer Gene Census, and what access requirements apply?

prompt_templates.title: Download a dataset
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through downloading GRCh38 coding mutation data with the included helper script. Include credential handling advice.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a gene
prompt_templates.prompt: After downloading the mutation export, help me filter records for TP53 and summarize useful fields.

prompt_templates.title: Design a pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a reproducible COSMIC ingestion workflow for mutations, signatures, fusions, and sample metadata across releases.

output_examples.input: I need the Cancer Gene Census file.
output: Recommended file: cancer_gene_census.csv under the GRCh38 COSMIC latest release.
The file supports cancer gene role filtering and evidence tier review.

output_examples.input: Which assembly should I use for a new study?
output_examples.output: Use GRCh38 for new work unless your existing pipeline requires GRCh37. Keep the COSMIC release version recorded for reproducibility.

output: Use the COSMIC signatures files for SBS, DBS, and indel reference profiles.
Record the signature version and COSMIC release used in the analysis.
Pair signature data with an appropriate downstream signature analysis tool.

best_practices: Use GRCh38 for new analyses unless a legacy pipeline requires GRCh37.
Prompt for COSMIC passwords securely instead of storing them in notebooks or shell history.
Record the COSMIC release version, file path, and citation with every downloaded dataset.
anti_patterns: Hardcoding COSMIC passwords in scripts, notebooks, or shared prompts.
Using latest in production pipelines without recording the resolved release.
Downloading full datasets when a targeted COSMIC file meets the research need.

faq.question: Do I need a COSMIC account?
faq.answer: Yes. COSMIC downloads require registered credentials from the Sanger COSMIC service.

faq.question: Can commercial teams use this skill?
faq.answer: Commercial users may need a QIAGEN license before downloading or using COSMIC data.

faq.question: Does the skill include COSMIC data?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and helper scripts. Data downloads require your own COSMIC access.

faq.question: Which file formats are covered?
faq.answer: The skill covers TSV, CSV, and VCF files, including compressed COSMIC download formats.

faq.question: Can it provide medical advice?
faq.answer: No. It supports research data access and analysis planning, not clinical decisions.

faq.question: What tools can use it?
faq.answer: The skill is prepared for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
